reductionDefinition: Karp's Reduction from Hitting Set to Exact Cover
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
complexity: O(subSets * universalSet), sizes of HITTINGSET's own sets

reductionFrom.formalDefinition: Hitting set family of subsets {U_i} of a set {S_j} where there is a set W such that, for each i, |W union U_i| = 1.
reductionFrom.problemDefinition: Hitting set is the problem of finding a set where it shares exactly one element with each subset U_i.
reductionFrom.inputDescription: U, a universal set, and S, a collection of subsets of U
reductionFrom.outputDescription: True or False, whether a hitting set exists that shares exactly one element with each subset in S
reductionFrom.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionFrom.instanceFormat: Format: {(U,S) | U is set, S subset {a | a subset U}} Example: ({1,2,3,4},{{1,3},{2,3,4},{1,4}})
reductionFrom.certificateFormat: Format: W subset U | W intersects every subset in S in exactly one element Example: {1,2}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Hitting Set

timeComplexity.Description: , n = |universalSet|, s = number of subsets in S

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Hitting Set

defaultVisualization.visualizationDefinition: This is a default visualization for Hitting Set

solver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for Hitting Set

timeComplexity.Description: , n = |universalSet|, s = number of subsets in S

reductionTo.formalDefinition: Exact Cover = {<S, X> | S is a collection of subsets of a set X where S* exists such that S* is a subcollection of S and an exact cover, of S. This means that each element of X is in exactly one subset of S*.}
reductionTo.problemDefinition: The exact cover problem is a decision problem to determine if an exact cover exists for some <S, X>
reductionTo.inputDescription: X, a set, and S, a collection of subsets of X
reductionTo.outputDescription: True or False, whether an exact cover of X exists using subsets from S
reductionTo.source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
reductionTo.instanceFormat: Format: {(U,S) | U is set, S subset {a | a subset U}} Example: ({1,2,3,4},{{1,2,3},{2,3},{4,1}})
reductionTo.certificateFormat: Format: {T | T subset S, union of T = X, T pairwise disjoint} Example: {{2,3},{4,1}}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a generic brute force solver for Exact Cover

defaultVerifier.verifierDefinition: This is a verifier for Exact Cover
